newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU aims to focus on positive in U.S. relations.
newsitem.headline: EU aims to focus on positive in U.S. relations.

text.p: Following a year of strained relations with the United States over trade policy, European Union foreign ministers want to start 1997 on the right foot by focusing on the high points of relations with Washington.

Diplomats said a meeting of EU foreign ministers in Brussels on Monday would stress the importance of maintaining good relations with Washington and repairing the cracks caused by the Helms-Burton row.
The EU was infuriated by what it saw as a rash of unacceptable extra-territorial laws emerging from Washington last year -- mainly involving trade with Cuba, Iran and Libya.

The Helms-Burton Act -- an amalgamation of decades of U.S. policy against Cuban leader Fidel Castro -- particularly incensed EU ministers as it threatened some European companies with punitive lawsuits unless they disinvested from Cuba.

Named after its congressional sponsors, Jesse Helms and Dan Burton, the act among other things allows naturalised Americans to sue in U.S. courts any European company or individual deemed to have benefited from investments in property confiscated since the Cuban communist revolution of 1959.

The EU responded by taking a complaint to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) -- where it is now being processed -- and also by swiftly enacting laws which bar Europeans from complying with Helms-Burton.
On January 3 U.S. President Bill Clinton suspended that part of the act for six months, ostensibly as a reward to Washington's allies for helping further isolate Havana.

But the threat of court action -- and similar action under the D'Amato Bill which seeks to isolate Iran and Libya -- remains and the Netherlands, current EU president under the rotating six-month system, is determined to push these issues onto the backburner.

Dutch diplomats have said they will be trying to stress the positive along the lines fixed by the New Transatlantic Agenda, an agreement between the EU and United States which outlines the scope for relations.
The next EU/U.S. summit takes place in the Hague in May and the Dutch are determined this meeting will trumpet the achievements and close links between the world's two biggest trading partners.

These include negotiations on mutual recognition agreements, the finalisation of an information technology agreement and the completion of a basic telecoms trade deal currently being negotiated at the WTO in Geneva.
Ministers will also on Monday highlight the growing political cooperation between the EU and Washington -- particularly in sensitive areas such as the Middle East and former Yugoslavia.
Monday's meeting will review last month's signing of a cooperation agreement with Canada which covers foreign policy, security, economic and commercial links.

Ministers are also to discuss the situation in the Great Lakes region of Africa, the Middle East, results of the WTO ministerial meeting in Singapore last year and the situation in Belarus and in former Yugoslavia.
